name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing and inauthentic network activity on social platforms, spanning the CooRnet/CLSB methodology, the VERA-AI Alert monitoring system, and case studies of information operations (e.g. the 'Zombie Internet' and gambling-promotion networks). This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains the most active current strand of work.

name: Platform Data Governance & Transparency
description: Research and policy engagement on social media platforms' data access regimes, API restrictions, and content-moderation policies under the Digital Service Act era — including work on Meta's URL Shares Dataset thresholds, political-content reduction policy, and service as a Digital Services Act / JRC expert on systemic platform risks.

name: Generative AI in Media and Disinformation
description: Study of generative AI both as a vector for deceptive persuasion (synthetic visual content in coordinated gambling promotion) and as a research tool for content analysis (LLM-in-the-loop pipelines, embedding-model comparisons for clustering political news). Reflects a fast-growing agenda mirrored in the new 'IA Generativa e Media' course.

name: Political Communication and Elections
description: Comparative and longitudinal study of social media dynamics around national elections (Italy 2018/2022, Germany 2021, Brazil post-Bolsonaro), covering partisan attention, affective community engagement, polarization, and hyperpartisan networks — the core empirical domain of the MINE programme.

name: Information Disorder and Fake News
description: Conceptual and empirical work on misinformation, disinformation and 'fake news' within hybrid media systems, including taxonomies of misleading information, PROMPT's narrative-monitoring dashboards, and reflections on the state of disinformation research and countermeasures.

name: Health Misinformation
description: Mapping of coordinated networks and alternative-influence structures spreading problematic health content, including COVID-19 fact-checking acceleration (MINE-FACTS), vaccine and pandemic-era information ecosystems in India and Nigeria, and online quack medicine discourse.

name: News Consumption in the Hybrid Media System
description: Studies of how news is produced, circulated and consumed across converging legacy and social media environments — insularity and cross-partisan sharing patterns, comparative newsfeed analysis across Europe, and the changing 'patchwork' of Italian media consumption.

name: Sociocybernetics and Social Systems Theory
description: A recurring theoretical strand linking Luhmannian social systems theory and sociocybernetics to internet and computational social science, addressed through ISA World Congress contributions and journal work bridging classical systems theory with digital media observation.

name: Social TV and Second-Screen Audiences
description: Earlier but foundational research line on Twitter-based second-screen participation around television events (talk shows, elections, media events), establishing the researcher's early expertise in large-scale social media data analysis later extended to disinformation research.

name: Platforms, Audiences, and Online Communities
description: Empirical and reflective studies of how platform affordances, cultures, and audience practices shape online sociality, identity, and community formation across sites like Facebook, TikTok, Instagram, Twitter/Mastodon, and LiveJournal.

name: Critical Analysis of AI Industry Imaginaries and Discourse
description: Studies examining how AI industry actors, media, and communities construct and circulate narratives, imaginaries, and framings (e.g., longtermism, techno-hagiography, 'quiet futuring', political-economy 'decoys') that shape public understanding and obscure or legitimize the underlying power structures of AI development.

name: Reflections on the State of Misinformation and Online Harm Research
description: Papers that step back from primary empirical study to critically assess the misinformation/online-harms research field itself — diagnosing biases (e.g., WEIRD-centrism, overreliance on cognitive proxies), mapping gaps in evidence (causal, longitudinal, cross-national), and proposing directions or borrowed lessons (e.g., from climate psychology) to make the field more rigorous and generalizable.

name: Theorizing AI's Social Role: Agency, Trust, and Public Perception
description: Papers that apply or extend social theory and communication-trust frameworks to understand the societal position of AI systems, ranging from conceptual demarcations of machine agency and formal multi-agent social frameworks to models of public trust in generative AI and empirical survey data on public attitudes toward AI adoption.

name: Computational Studies of Political Media and Advertising
description: Papers using large-scale computational or quasi-experimental methods to study political advertising, media capture, and ideological signaling on digital platforms, including causal analysis of ad effects, detection of covert advertiser influence on news coverage, and latent ideology estimation of political video content.

name: Survey Measurement Validity and Comparability
description: Papers examining methodological challenges in survey-based measurement, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how online sample composition and quality checks affect representativeness and response validity, and how question wording and dataset differences affect cross-national and longitudinal comparability of trust measures.
